## Master Directory Structure

```
project-root/
├── package.json                     # Vite + three deps, no physics/game-engine libs
├── vite.config.js                   # multi-entry build (one HTML entry per game)
├── index.html                       # launcher/menu linking to each game build
├── README.md
│
├── shared/                          # reusable across the whole collection
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── GameEngine.js            # scene/camera/renderer bootstrap, fixed-timestep loop
│   │   ├── InputManager.js          # unified keyboard + Gamepad API polling, action-mapped
│   │   ├── StateMachine.js          # generic FSM (menu/playing/paused/gameover)
│   │   └── ObjectPool.js            # generic typed pool (acquire/release/grow)
│   │
│   ├── vfx/                         # the six mandatory shared VFX systems
│   │   ├── CameraShake.js           # trauma-based, decaying, velocity-scaled
│   │   ├── ParticleManager.js       # InstancedMesh-backed, hard cap 500, pooled
│   │   ├── HitStop.js               # timescale dilation on heavy impacts
│   │   ├── MotionTrail.js           # ribbon-geometry trails for fast movers
│   │   ├── ShockwaveRing.js         # pooled expanding emissive ring meshes
│   │   └── FloatingText.js          # pooled 3D/CSS2D score-popup text
│   │
│   ├── audio/
│   │   ├── AudioEngine.js           # Web Audio context, master bus, compressor
│   │   ├── SynthVoice.js            # oscillator+envelope primitives
│   │   └── SFXLibrary.js            # presets built from SynthVoice (per-game reuse)
│   │
│   ├── procgen/
│   │   ├── NoiseField.js            # hand-written simplex noise
│   │   ├── CanvasTextureFactory.js  # Canvas API procedural textures
│   │   └── GeometryDisplace.js      # vertex displacement helpers (noise/sine)
│   │
│   ├── postfx/
│   │   └── PostProcessingStack.js   # EffectComposer + UnrealBloomPass, tuned presets
│   │
│   ├── physics/
│   │   └── CollisionMath.js         # AABB/circle/ray-cast, vanilla, no physics engine
│   │
│   ├── ui/
│   │   ├── glass.css                # glassmorphism tokens + neon-glow variants
│   │   └── HUD.js                   # score/lives/overlay scaffold, DOM-based
│   │
│   └── utils/
│       ├── MathUtils.js
│       ├── Constants.js
│       └── Disposer.js              # tracks + disposes geometries/materials/textures
│
└── [GameName]/                      # exactly-named folder, created only when commanded
    ├── index.html                   # Vite entry for this game
    ├── main.js                      # boots GameEngine, wires InputManager, starts loop
    ├── plan.md                      # produced in Step 2, specific to this game
    ├── scenes/                      # arena/level construction
    ├── entities/                    # player, enemies, projectiles (pooled)
    └── systems/                     # game-specific logic (scoring, waves, AI, etc.)
```

**Vite setup:** each `[GameName]/index.html` is its own Vite entry point (multi-page build via `build.rollupOptions.input`); the root `index.html` is a launcher. `shared/` is imported by relative or aliased path (`@shared/...` via `vite.config.js` resolve alias) so no game reaches across another game's folder.

**Shared-utilities strategy:** every system a game *might* need (input, pooling, VFX, audio synthesis, post-processing, collision math) lives in `shared/` as engine-agnostic-to-genre modules. A game folder only ever *composes* these — it never duplicates pooling, shake, or bloom setup locally. Anything genre-specific (grid logic, wave spawning, maze pathing) stays inside that game's own `systems/`.

**Compliance:**
- **Anti-Lazy Directive:** understood — Step 3 will contain zero placeholder comments or elisions; every function shipped complete.
- **Strict Memory Management:** understood — all pooled objects reused via `ObjectPool`/`ParticleManager`, and `Disposer.js` will track every geometry/material/texture created outside a pool for explicit `.dispose()` on teardown.
- **Sequential Output Protocol:** understood — no files created, no commands run this step; Step 2 begins only on "Begin [Game Name]," Step 3 only on "Plan approved," and any truncated file resumes verbatim on "continue."
